traceability.evidence: Story file docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md exists and defines deep-validation requirements REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, REQ-DEEP-SECTION, REQ-DEEP-CACHE, and REQ-DEEP-ERROR. The ESLint rule src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts is explicitly annotated with @story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md and implements deep requirement validation: it parses JSDoc comments to find @story, @req, and @implements annotations (functions extractStoryPath, extractReqIdFromLine, handleAnnotationLine, processCommentLines, processAllComments), validates and resolves story paths with security checks (validateAndResolveStoryPath, plus messageId 'invalidPath'), reads story files and extracts all requirement IDs using a generic /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g regex and caches them per story path (loadAndCacheRequirements with a shared Map reqCache, satisfying REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, REQ-DEEP-SECTION, REQ-DEEP-CACHE), and checks that each referenced requirement exists in the corresponding story file (checkRequirementExists, validateReqLine, validateImplementsLine, satisfying REQ-DEEP-MATCH). The rule exposes clear error messages via meta.messages: 'reqMissing: Requirement {{reqId}} not found in {{storyPath}}' and 'invalidPath: Invalid story path {{storyPath}}', fulfilling the User Experience and REQ-DEEP-ERROR criteria. Integration with the plugin is confirmed in src/index.ts, where RULE_NAMES includes 'valid-req-reference', the rule is dynamically required into the exported rules object, and TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps 'traceability/valid-req-reference' to 'error' so it runs in recommended/strict configs alongside existing annotation and file-validation rules. Tests in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts are explicitly tagged as 'Tests for: docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md' and use RuleTester to cover: valid references into docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md; bullet-style requirements via tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md; multi-story and shared IDs via tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md with @implements; and invalid cases for missing requirements and invalid paths that assert the exact 'reqMissing' and 'invalidPath' messages and data payloads. Fixtures tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md, story_multi_a.md, and story_multi_b.md demonstrate support for different markdown structures (bulleted requirements, multiple stories with shared IDs), confirming that the generic regex-based parser works across formats and sections. User/developer documentation in README.md and docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md describes this rule as enforcing that @req and @implements annotations reference existing requirements in story files, explains its deep-validation behavior (file existence, parsing, matching, error messages), and provides concrete examples of correct and incorrect usage, satisfying the Documentation acceptance criterion.
traceability.notes: The deep requirement-content validation requested by story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION is fully implemented by the 'valid-req-reference' ESLint rule and its surrounding infrastructure. The rule parses annotations, resolves and secures story paths, lazily reads and caches story-file requirements, and verifies that every @req and @implements requirement ID exists in the referenced story file, emitting clear, specific diagnostics when it does not. Tests directly tied to this story exercise both happy-path and failure scenarios across multiple story-file formats (normal .story.md requirements and bullet-list fixtures) and multi-story cases, while plugin integration and dedicated documentation confirm that the behavior is wired into normal usage and clearly explained. All acceptance criteria, including core functionality, support for varied formats/structures, integration with existing validation logic, clear error reporting, graceful handling via caching and path checks, and documentation with examples, are effectively satisfied.
